title: Adjoint differential and centrality of the adjoint kernel in characteristic zero
statement: Let $k$ be a field of characteristic zero [def-weil-field], and let $G$ be a smooth connected affine $k$-group scheme of finite type [def-sc-group-scheme, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-connected-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. The tangent space $\mathfrak g=T_{G/k,e}$ [def-sc-scheme-tangent-space], with the bracket induced by group commutators, is a finite-dimensional $k$-Lie algebra [def-wf-lie-algebra]. Let $\operatorname{Ad}:G\to\operatorname{GL}(\mathfrak g)$ be the representation given by differentiating conjugation, where $\operatorname{GL}(\mathfrak g)(A)=\operatorname{Aut}_A(\mathfrak g\otimes_k A)$ for a commutative $k$-algebra $A$. Identifying the tangent space of this general linear group with $\operatorname{End}_k(\mathfrak g)$, one has $d\operatorname{Ad}_e(X)(Y)=[X,Y]$. The scheme-theoretic kernel $N=\ker\operatorname{Ad}$ is the centre $Z(G)$ [lem-sfb-affine-group-centre-base-change]. In particular, for every commutative $k$-algebra $A$, every $n\in N(A)$ and every $g\in G(A)$, one has $ng=gn$. The assertion includes nonreduced $A$ and the case $\mathfrak g=0$.

source.place: Theorem 10.23 and Remark 10.24, printed pp.193-194 (Lie bracket and differential of Ad); Proposition 10.15, pp.190-191, Proposition 10.31, p.196, and Cartier Theorem 3.23, p.71, applied over an algebraic closure to centralizers of elements in ker Ad. Proposition 1.92, pp.33-34, and the subsequent base-change paragraph give the scheme centre. The characteristic-zero kernel equality is an agent-stated corollary, not Proposition 10.33 alone.

proof.text: Put $C=k[G]$, with comultiplication $\Delta$, counit $\varepsilon$ and antipode $S$ supplied by [lem-sfb-affine-group-coordinate-hopf], and $I=\ker\varepsilon$. By [lem-pc-affine-finite-type-algebra], choose algebra generators $c_1,\ldots,c_r$ of $C$. Polynomial expansion modulo $I^2$ shows that the classes of $c_i-\varepsilon(c_i)$ span $I/I^2$. The derivation identification in [lem-sfb-bialgebra-distribution-tangent-calculus] identifies $\mathfrak g$ with $(I/I^2)^\vee$; the Lie structure and finite dimensionality are also stated in [lem-sfb-affine-group-lie-tangent-calculus]. For any commutative $k$-algebra $A$, an infinitesimal point is a map $C\to A[t]/t^2$, $c\mapsto\varepsilon(c)+tD(c)$. Multiplicativity is precisely $D(cd)=\varepsilon(c)D(d)+D(c)\varepsilon(d)$, equivalently $D$ factors linearly through $I/I^2$. A finite basis of $I/I^2$ therefore identifies these points with $\operatorname{Hom}_k(I/I^2,A)=\mathfrak g\otimes_k A$, naturally in $A$. The product corresponds to addition: evaluating $\Delta$ gives $\varepsilon(c)+t(D(c)+E(c))$, by its two counit identities. Indeed, multiplying $(\varepsilon+uX)*(\varepsilon+vY)*(\varepsilon-uX)*(\varepsilon-vY)$ with $u^2=v^2=0$ gives $\varepsilon+uv(X*Y-Y*X)$. Thus the bracket of mixed commutators is the convolution bracket in the cited distribution lemma.

Conjugation by $a\in G(A)$ acts on the infinitesimal points of step 1. On the corresponding derivations its formula is
$$(\operatorname{Ad}(a)X)(c)=\sum a(c_{(1)})X(c_{(2)})a(S(c_{(3)})),$$
where the triple tensor is $(\Delta\otimes1)\Delta(c)$ [lem-sfb-affine-group-coordinate-hopf]. Conjugation fixes the identity, so the formula preserves the counit derivation rule, and it is $A$-linear in $X$. Conjugation by $a^{-1}$ is its inverse. In a finite basis of $\mathfrak g$, apply this formula to the universal point $C\to C$: its matrix entries belong to $C$, and the inverse matrix also has entries in $C$. Their determinant is thus a unit. The affine morphism correspondence [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-into-affine-scheme] gives a morphism $G\to\operatorname{GL}(\mathfrak g)$. Composition of conjugations gives its group law on every algebra, so it is the claimed representation. For $a=\varepsilon+tX$, its convolution inverse is $\varepsilon-tX$; hence its action on $Y$ is
$$(\varepsilon+tX)*Y*(\varepsilon-tX)=Y+t(X*Y-Y*X)=Y+t[X,Y].$$
The last equality is exactly the bracket formula of [lem-sfb-bialgebra-distribution-tangent-calculus]. The characterization of the tangent map to a general linear group in [lem-sfb-affine-group-lie-tangent-calculus] now gives $d\operatorname{Ad}_e(X)(Y)=[X,Y]$.

The kernel $N$ is a closed subgroup by [lem-sc-kernel-subgroup]. Explicitly its ideal in $C$ is generated by the entries of the universal matrix $\operatorname{Ad}-1$; thus its coordinate algebra is finitely generated, being a quotient of $C$. This description gives $N(A)=\ker\operatorname{Ad}(A)$ for every $A$, and after any field extension the same equations define the corresponding kernel. Let $Z=Z(G)$ be the closed subgroup of [lem-sfb-affine-group-centre-base-change]. If $z\in Z(A)$, its image commutes with every point of $G(A[t]/t^2)$, by that node's universal centre condition. In particular it fixes every infinitesimal point in step 1; hence $\operatorname{Ad}(z)=1$ on $\mathfrak g\otimes_k A$. This proves $Z\subseteq N$ on all algebras. The ideal description of a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion] makes these inclusions inclusions of closed subgroup schemes.

source.place: 10.33, displayed inclusion (64), printed p.197; Proposition 1.92, pp.33--34

proof.text: Fix any field extension $K/k$ and any $n\in N(K)$. The identity section and [lem-sbc-connected-rational-point-geometrically-connected] show that $G_K$ is connected. Its coordinate algebra is finitely generated by the images of the generators of $C$. It is smooth by [lem-sfb-char-zero-affine-group-smooth]. By the natural tangent identification of [lem-sfb-affine-group-lie-tangent-calculus] and the formula of step 2, the differential of conjugation $c_n$ on $G_K$ is $\operatorname{Ad}(n)=1$. Form its fixed subscheme $H\subseteq G_K$: in $B=K[G_K]$ it is cut out by $c_n^*(b)-b$ for all $b\in B$ [def-weil-closed-immersion]. On every $K$-algebra its points are exactly the elements commuting with $n$, so they form a subgroup [def-sc-group-scheme-subgroup]. The quotient of $B$ is finitely generated. A tangent point $t_X$ belongs to $H$ exactly when $c_n(t_X)=t_X$, equivalently $\operatorname{Ad}(n)X=X$. Thus $\operatorname{Lie}(H)=\operatorname{Lie}(G_K)$. Apply [lem-sfb-charzero-lie-detects-factorization] to $f=\mathrm{id}_{G_K}$ and $H\hookrightarrow G_K$. All its hypotheses hold; it imposes no smoothness condition on $H$. The identity factors through $H$, so $H=G_K$. In particular $n$ commutes with every element of $G(K)$. This argument works for every extension field, not just an algebraic closure.

source.place: Proposition 10.15, pp.190--191 and Cartier Theorem 3.23, p.71; centre argument following 1.92, pp.33--34

proof.text: Consider the group scheme $P=N\times_kG$, whose coordinate algebra is the tensor product of two finitely generated $k$-algebras, hence is finitely generated by their two finite sets of generators. It is an affine finite-type group under componentwise multiplication [def-sc-group-scheme]. By [lem-sfb-char-zero-affine-group-smooth] it is smooth, and [sbc-lem-smooth-geometrically-reduced] makes $P$ reduced (the unique fibre over $\operatorname{Spec}k$ is $P$). Let $q:P\to G$ be $q(n,g)=ngn^{-1}g^{-1}$. For each scheme point $p$ of $P$, its canonical residue-field point is a pair $(n,g)$ over $K=\kappa(p)$; step 4 says $q(n,g)=e$. Therefore the set-theoretic image of $q$ is contained in the identity section $e:\operatorname{Spec}k\hookrightarrow G$, which is closed: on $C$ it is the quotient $C\twoheadrightarrow C/I=k$ [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-source-factors-through-closed-subscheme] to $q$, this closed immersion and the reduced source $P$. It yields $q=e\circ(P\to\operatorname{Spec}k)$ as morphisms. Thus for every algebra $A$, $n\in N(A)$ and $g\in G(A)$ commute, and the same holds after every $A$-algebra extension. The universal centre condition of [lem-sfb-affine-group-centre-base-change] gives $N\subseteq Z(G)$. Together with step 3 this proves the scheme-theoretic equality. No argument required $A$ reduced or $\dim\mathfrak g>0$: in dimension zero the matrices in step 2 are empty with determinant $1$, and the rest of the argument is unchanged.

lean.statement: theorem exists_charZero_adjoint_differential_central_kernel {k : Type u} [Field k] [CharZero k] (G : Grp (Over (Spec (.of k)))) (hG : SolvableGroupStructure.IsAlgebraic G) (hsm : Smooth G.X.hom) (hc : ConnectedSpace G.X.left) : ∃ (n : ℕ) (b : Module.Basis (ULift.{u} (Fin n)) k (GrpObj.Lie G.X)) (r : G ⟶ Grp.mk (GeneralLinearGroup (ULift.{u} (Fin n)) k)), (∀ (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [Algebra k A] (g : points G.X A) (v : ULift.{u} (Fin n) → A), adjointBasisTangentPoint G.X b A ((GeneralLinearGroup.RationalHom.points r.hom.hom A g).val.mulVec v) = points.map G.X (TrivSqZeroExt.inlAlgHom k A A) g * adjointBasisTangentPoint G.X b A v * (points.map G.X (TrivSqZeroExt.inlAlgHom k A A) g)⁻¹) ∧ (∀ X Y : GrpObj.Lie G.X, (GeneralLinearGroup.RationalHom.differential r.hom.hom X).mulVec (b.equivFun Y) = b.equivFun ⁅X, Y⁆) ∧ (∀ (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [Algebra k A], Set.range (fun x : StandardGroupSchemes.affine k A ⟶ GrpObj.ker r.hom.hom ↦ x ≫ GrpObj.kerι r.hom.hom) = ReductiveTorusCentralizer.centralizerPoints (𝟙 G) A) ∧ ∀ (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [Algebra k A] (x : StandardGroupSchemes.affine k A ⟶ GrpObj.ker r.hom.hom) (g : StandardGroupSchemes.affine k A ⟶ G.X), Commute (x ≫ GrpObj.kerι r.hom.hom) g
